datatype_registry_deep_dive.summary: Two-registry model confirmed with precise function evidence.

primary_registry.mechanism: Reads entities/defs/alias.xml, calls DataType_BuildFromSection for each child, inserts name->DataType* into std::map via StdMap_DataType_EmplaceOrFind
primary_registry.queried_by: DataType_BuildFromSection @ 0x01597150 (for type lookup during entity .def parsing)

secondary_registry.mechanism: Lazy-allocates object via scalable_malloc(0xc) + FUN_00460320 (map ctor). Calls vtable[1] to get type name. Checks for duplicates via FUN_0158ea90 (map find). Inserts via FUN_00476590 (map operator[]). Logs 'MetaDataType::addType: %s has already been registered' on duplicate.

datatype_registry_deep_dive.interaction_model: The two registries serve different lookup paths: (1) DataType_BuildFromSection queries g_mapDataTypeRegistry when building a DataType from an XML section tag name (the alias.xml-derived map maps tag string -> DataType* factory). (2) DataType_LookupByName queries g_pMetaDataTypeRegistry using the C++ type's runtime name (the MetaDataType map maps type name -> SimpleMetaDataType<T>* instance). These are NOT the same lookup: alias.xml creates aliases like 'INT8'->IntegerDataType<signed_char>, while the MetaDataType registry stores 'INT8'->'unsigned char' (the C++ template instantiation name). They can have different keys for the same underlying type.
datatype_registry_deep_dive.clarification_of_w4b2_ambiguity: W4-B2 noted that DataType_LookupByName reads DAT_01f126b4 and called it 'g_mapDataTypeRegistryLookup' — but this is the SAME address as g_pMetaDataTypeRegistry (the secondary registry). There are only two registry objects: g_mapDataTypeRegistry at 01f126b8 (primary std::map with alias.xml entries) and g_pMetaDataTypeRegistry at 01f126b4 (secondary std::map with MetaDataType ctor entries). The pending_globals 'g_mapDataTypeRegistryLookup' and 'g_pMetaDataTypeRegistry' are the SAME global — both DAT_01f126b4.

md5_system.purpose: Type signature hashing. Each DataType's GetTypeName-WriteStream method calls MD5_Update with binary encoding of the type (e.g. uint8=1, uint16=2, float='Float', etc.). Used to produce unique type IDs for entity protocol versioning. DAT_01b1bd58 is the MD5 state buffer.

cme_property_system.summary: CME::Detail::PropertyNode hierarchy — 14 typed property wrapper classes mirroring the 14 BigWorld DataType primitives. Used for runtime property serialization/deserialization separate from BigWorld's stream-based protocol. TypeList covers: uint8, int8, uint16, int16, uint32, int32, uint64, int64, float, wstring, Vector2, Vector3, Vector4 + NullType terminator.

sub_slot_encoding_status: NOT YET VERIFIED in this range. The sub-slot check function from BigWorld 2.0.1 entity_method_descriptions.cpp::checkExposedForSubSlots() relates to SGWPlayer's 157 client methods with sub-slot encoding at 62+. This system sits in the EntityDescription method assignment functions already covered by W4-B1 (EntityDescription_AssignClientMethodIds @ 0x01590df0, EntityDescription_DecodeClientMethodId @ 0x01590ee0). Those functions encode using multi-byte IDs when count >= 0x3e=62. The threshold constant 0x3e matches the BigWorld 2.0.1 sub-slot boundary exactly. CONCLUSION: sub-slot behavior is CONFIRMED via W4-B1's findings. No new evidence in this high-half range changes this conclusion.

Three subsystems: (1) Type initializer helpers (015ac070-015ac7a0): tiny init functions for RPC struct objects of varying sizes. (2) Message serializer stubs (015abfd0-015b2410): ~170 functions with signature (uint ctx, char* key, int type, T* val, byte* schema). Each writes a typed field via FUN_00a4a650/a4ad10/a3c260 etc. Type codes: 0x7c=PointSetCommitResponse, 0x80=PointSetCommit2Response, 0x84=PointSetCheckoutResponse, 0x88=PointSetBrowseResponse, 0x8b=PointSetBrowse, 0x8c=PointSetBrowseToPointResponse, 0x8f=PointSetBrowseToPoint, 0x90=PointSetGetSelectionResponse, 0x94=PointSetGetSelection, 0x95=AvatarSetCreateResponse, 0x9a=AvatarSetModResponse, 0xa1=AvatarSetGet, 0xa2=AvatarSetGetDetailResponse, etc. Master dispatch at 015b2410 (huge switch statement on type code, maps 0x01-0xa5 to named unrpc: types). (3) RPC command handlers (015bbd80-015bfe70): uniform handler pattern (FUN_00a45be0 entry check, flag at +0x154f6, FUN_00a3b680 context alloc, inner XML attribute readers, FUN_015abad0 state machine loop, FUN_00a436c0 close).
